sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS CREDIT CARDS.  FIND OUT HOW THE OTHER CALLER MAKES USE OF CREDIT CARDS.  HOW DO THEY COMPARE TO YOUR OWN?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Yeah, you want to chat about credit cards?
ParticipantB: Sure, yeah. I mean, I do use them, but it's kind of... it's a big part of my life now.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? Mine is mostly just for the big stuff. Like the car or the house.
ParticipantB: That's different from me. I use mine for groceries and gas and stuff every single day.
ParticipantA: Hmm. Well, I guess I get why. It's easy to just swipe instead of digging into cash.
ParticipantB: Exactly. But I have this cousin who works at a bank, and she keeps telling me to be careful.
ParticipantA: Oh? What does she say?
ParticipantB: She says I'm building a huge nest egg of debt. She says I shouldn't keep balances so high if I don't pay them off.
ParticipantA: That actually scares me a little bit. I know I shouldn't carry a balance, but sometimes the interest rates are just... steep.
ParticipantB: Yeah, my cousin says the same thing. She told me once, "If you can't pay it in full next month, you're paying someone else to borrow your money."
ParticipantA: That stings. I mean, I have some debts I don't want to get rid of right now. My payments are just... manageable, but they add up.
ParticipantB: I get that. My cousin says you have to live within your means, though. She says if you spend what you don't have, it catches up to you eventually.
ParticipantA: True. I guess I just feel like I'm okay because I can pay the minimums, even if it hurts a little bit.
ParticipantB: Well, my cousin says that's a trap. She says it keeps you in a cycle where you never actually save anything.
ParticipantA: Maybe she's right. I mean, I don't have an emergency fund or anything. That's probably why I feel so stuck sometimes.
ParticipantB: Yeah. My cousin actually helped me set up a budget a while back. She showed me how to track everything.
ParticipantA: Really? Oh, that sounds helpful. I never really did that. I just let the bills roll in.
ParticipantB: Well, I try to do it now. I pay off my gas card by the 1st of every month, and I try not to touch the other stuff unless it's an emergency.
ParticipantA: That's smart. I feel like I've been doing it my way for years, and maybe it's not the best way.
ParticipantB: It's not, honestly. My cousin says credit cards are great tools if you use them right, but they're dangerous if you don't watch them.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I think I need to talk to her. Maybe I'll try to get my balances down to zero next month.
ParticipantB: You should. It feels so much lighter when you don't owe anything.
ParticipantA: Exactly. I feel relieved just thinking about it.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Well, I guess we're kind of different. You're the cautious type, and I'm the... well, I'm learning to be more cautious.
ParticipantA: True. I think I'll stick with just the big purchases for now, and maybe stop using the card for daily stuff.
ParticipantB: That's a good start. My cousin says that's a huge step.
ParticipantA: Okay, well, I'm glad I asked you. Thanks for chatting.
ParticipantB: Sure thing. Good luck with your budgeting.
ParticipantA: Will do. Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
